headline: NQ is in the CME weekend halt with no live price path: Tail stays low at 9% and EA_ON, while Stress holds elevated at 45% on a 5% weekly oil rally, a sharp consumer-data miss and an Iran sanctions package now flagged for next week.
body: No live price path is available this hour. CME equity-index futures closed for the weekend at Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and do not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, so directional efficiency, pullback depth, repeated extension and proximity to session extremes are all unobservable for the whole of the current 24-hour horizon. Everything below is the last confirmed state plus corroborated news, and that limitation - not a judgement that markets are calm - is what caps Confidence below the solid band. Last confirmed structure (Friday 14 August U.S. cash session): the Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,046.14, down 38.36 points or 0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 session range and roughly 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20. Closing mid-range rather than pinned at an extreme is the single most important structural fact available, and it argues directly against pathological one-way structure. The S&P 500 closed at 7,785.76 (-0.17%), the Nasdaq Composite at 26,729.16 (-0.28%) and the Dow at 53,732.41 (-0.20%), all slipping from Thursday's record close while still capping a third consecutive weekly gain. VIX closed at 14.25, down 2.60% - a level entirely inconsistent with a stressed or one-way tape. Macro was the drag and it was a genuine miss on both prints: July retail sales fell 0.6% month-on-month against expectations of +0.1%, the largest decline in over a year, and the University of Michigan preliminary August sentiment index printed 51 against 55.2 prior and a forecast near 55, with one-year inflation expectations rising to 4.3%. Company-level pressure was concentrated rather than broad: Broadcom fell about 6% on Bank of America scrutiny of proposed debt-financing structures, Applied Materials fell despite beating on revenue and adjusted EPS, and Reddit rose about 13% on pending S&P 500 inclusion. Energy and basic materials outperformed while technology and healthcare weighed, in what the tape was described as low-volume summer trading. Cross-asset: WTI settled at $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent at $88.59 (+1.75%), extending a roughly 5% weekly gain on the Hormuz closure and an IEA warning about deeper global supply deficits. On rates the evidence is slightly inconsistent and is reported as such - the Federal Reserve H.15 release dated 14 August shows 13 August constant-maturity yields of 4.15% at 2 years and 4.63% at 10 years, while Friday's market reporting put the 10-year near 4.69%; the more telling datapoint is that a 30-year auction cleared at 5.216%, the highest in 25 years, pointing to real long-end pressure. Geopolitics remains the one live channel during the halt. The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since late February under a U.S. naval blockade, with tanker strikes including a UAE-flagged ADNOC vessel the UAE attributes to Iran. Treasury Secretary Bessent said the administration will apply measures 'like have never been seen in the history of economic isolation on a country', combined with continued blockade enforcement - and, importantly for timing, he flagged the announcement for next week rather than for this weekend. In the other direction, Iran's foreign minister has said an Oman shipping agreement is close, though conditioned on sanctions relief and reparations. Interpretation: the signals genuinely conflict, which is why this is scored as elevated Stress with low Tail rather than as either calm or dangerous. Equity volatility pricing near 14, index levels close to records, a mid-range orderly Friday close and a third straight weekly gain argue against imminent pathological structure. A closed chokepoint, oil up 5% on the week, a sharp consumer-demand and sentiment miss, a 25-year-high long-bond auction yield, a pending unprecedented sanctions package and a wobble in semiconductor leadership argue that the environment is difficult and gap-prone. Per the contract, conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail, and Stress should not decay to a trivial floor merely because the venue is shut while the catalyst set is unresolved - hence 45% here. Tail remains low at 9% because not one of the required Tail conditions - observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed pullbacks, repeated extension, NQ pinned near extremes - can be evidenced while no price is printing, and none was present at the last observable close.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 9-12% through the Asian and European sessions and easing to 7-9% across Friday's U.S. cash session: the softer Retail Sales and University of Michigan prints and the Broadcom/Applied Materials drag produced two-way volatility, not directional efficiency. Stress described a clear event arc - roughly 23-30% in the quiet pre-dawn hours, building to 41-44% through the U.S. cash session as the data and semiconductor news landed, then 34% after the 21:00 UTC weekly close and collapsing to 12% in the two post-close halt runs. That collapse is the reading the current assessment continues to correct: the venue shut, but the Hormuz closure, the oil rally and the pending sanctions package did not resolve, so the backdrop never justified a weekend floor. Confidence trended down through the day from the high 40s to the low 30s as live structure disappeared and supplementary data coverage degraded, recovering to the 50s in the early afternoon when primary-source reads succeeded. The 20:00 UTC slot has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable. Past hours are reproduced exactly as published and are not restated with later information.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it ends at 23:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August, still roughly 23 hours before the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August - so no scheduled U.S. macro release and no tradable price path fall within it. Tail is therefore projected flat at 9% for most of the window, ticking up to 10-11% only in the final slots as the reopen comes into view; this reflects accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays in the low band so the action is EA_ON green throughout. Stress is projected to ease from 45% to about 41% through the thin Saturday Asian and European hours, when Gulf-related headline flow is historically lightest, then firm back to 45% into the late slots as unresolved weekend headlines converge on the Sunday gap; it stays inside the elevated band all horizon because the oil rally, the consumer-demand miss and the pending Iran package are unresolved rather than because any event is scheduled. Confidence decays from 57% to 46% as Friday's verified evidence ages with nothing observable to replace it. The named danger window is the Sunday reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which sits just beyond this horizon; the next scheduled macro checkpoint is FOMC Minutes on 19 August at 18:00 UTC, with the Jackson Hole symposium falling on 27-29 August, outside the seven-day event window.
